summary: This bill requires large vehicle manufacturers to include specific drunk and impaired driving prevention technology in at least 10,000 passenger vehicles annually, based on either the DADSS Subsystem Performance Specification Document or the European New Car Assessment Programme standards, until a new federal rule on such technology takes effect.

scores.thoughts: This bill mandates that certain large vehicle manufacturers produce a minimum number of vehicles with drunk and impaired driving prevention technology. While this could lead to increased costs for manufacturers, it does not directly involve government spending or appropriations. The Secretary of Transportation has a role in reviewing standards, but this is an administrative function not tied to new spending.
